name: Proficiency
summary: One bonus, from your level alone, added to the handful of things you are trained in — and to nothing else.

sections.heading: One number, and it comes from your level
paragraphs: Your proficiency bonus is the same number for everything you are trained in, and it depends on your LEVEL alone — never on an ability, never on a class. A 5th-level Sandow and a 5th-level Illusionist both add +3.
It is already included in every number the sheet prints. You never add it twice, and you never add it by hand: if a box on your sheet shows +6, the proficiency is in there.

sections.heading: Where it applies
paragraphs: Four places, and you can read all four off your sheet.
list: SKILLS you are trained in — the two you chose at creation. A trained check is d20 + the skill's ability modifier + your proficiency bonus.
SAVING THROWS your class is good at — two of the six, shown as gold boxes in the Abilities row. The other four are the bare ability modifier.
ATTACKS with a weapon your class is proficient with — the to-hit only.
YOUR TRICK NUMBERS, if you cast: your trick save DC is 8 + proficiency + your class's ability, and a trick that makes an attack roll is d20 + proficiency + that same ability.

sections.heading: Where it does not
paragraphs: This is the half people get wrong, so it is worth saying plainly.
An UNTRAINED skill check is not forbidden — anyone may try to climb a rope or read a room. It is simply the ability modifier with nothing added. Being untrained costs you the bonus, not the attempt.
Proficiency is never added to DAMAGE, never to your ARMOUR CLASS, and never to your PARRY roll — a Parry is a flat d20 with no modifiers at all, which is the whole point of it (see Parry).

sections.heading: How you get a skill
paragraphs: At creation, from your class's own list: choose TWO. That is the only source of skill training in this system — there are no backgrounds handing out extra proficiencies, and levelling up grants none. Your background is your character's story, not a package of numbers.

So the two you pick are the two you have, for good. Pick them for the game you expect to play rather than for the class you are reading about: Perception is the check a DM calls for most often at any table, and every class in this company can take it.

sections.heading: Tools and armour
paragraphs: Your class also lists TOOLS you are proficient with — a disguise kit, a marionettist's kit, a playing card set. Add your proficiency bonus to a check made using one. What that check is for is a matter between you and your DM: this system does not publish a table of tool DCs, because a tool is an excuse for a scene rather than a subsystem.

ARMOUR proficiency works differently and carries no bonus at all — it is permission, not arithmetic. Your class names the categories you may wear, the creator offers you only those, and clothing needs no proficiency from anybody (see Armor & AC). There is deliberately no published penalty for wearing something you are not trained in, because there is no way in this app to end up wearing it; if it comes up at your table, it is the DM's call like everything else the app declines to judge.

sections.heading: No expertise here
paragraphs: There is no doubled proficiency in this system, and nothing grants half of one. One bonus, one size, the same for everybody at your level — which is what makes it safe for the app to fold it into every number without asking you which version you have.
